attempts.summary: Configured node1 (OPNsense) to route between two new subnets, lan-a (10.50.1.0/24, opt1/vtnet1, connected to node2) and lan-b (10.50.2.0/24, opt2/vtnet2, connected to node3), which were previously unconfigured second NICs. Created a single OPNsense port alias "node3_allowed_tcp_ports" (8080,8443,9000) and one firewall rule on interface lan-a permitting node2 (10.50.1.10) to reach node3 (10.50.2.10) over TCP on that alias — pf expands this into per-port rules sharing one rule label, confirming the alias is doing the port-set expansion rather than three hand-written rules. Also opened the same 3 ports in node3's local firewalld zone, since OPNsense's rule only governs the inter-subnet hop. Verified end-to-end TCP connectivity on all three ports and confirmed an unlisted port (7000) remains blocked (default-deny). Completed the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol: captured healthy baselines, restarted node2 then node3 (Linux boot_id changed) then node1 (OPNsense kern.boottime changed) one at a time via native reboot commands, polled until each node's exec access returned, and re-verified interface config, routes, firewalld ports, the pf alias-derived rule, and live TCP connectivity all fully recovered after each restart.
